E V E N   M O R E   M A I L !


   February, 1992    Page  Reply

 Ian Ross.............02    15

 Marc Broster.........21    26

 Ron Fox..............31    32

 Malcolm Perry........33    42

 Bill Coats...........46    50

From: Iain Ross

    LEARNING TO LIVE WITH SAM

SAM was brought to my notice
first by its rapturous welcome
by FORMAT which seemed to hail
it as the 'Second Coming' and
then by a series of decidedly
salty comments from OUTLET. My
decision not to buy what looked
like a can of worms was overcome
partly by very full information
and advice from one of FORMAT's
leading contributors and partly
by the growing feeling that the
Spectrum is inevitably, and
sadly, destined for oblivion. A
walk down Tottenham Court Road
last summer yielded not a trace
of the Spectrum nor any of its
accessories or software.

Needless to say, Ataris and
Amigas proliferated but buying
one would have lost me my
Specrum software. So last
September, at the Glasgow All
Formats Fair, I took the plunge
and treated myself to a 512K
SAM, two disc drives, a 1 Mb
extension, printer extension, a
mouse, Masterdos, Specmaker and
Speclone.


I use a computer essentially as
a piece of office equipment,
also as a means of indulging my
fondness for graphic art and
typography. Lacking technical
expertise and with no real prog-
ramming ability, I anticipated
lots of trouble and frustration.

In fact, apart from trouble with
a disc drive, virtually nothing
went wrong.

Not a keen computer buff, I left
SAM BASIC alone. Fascinated by
the extremely compact discdrives
hidden inside the computer, I
made these the first object of
my attention. One of the drives
worked; the other worked only
sporadically.


Numerous telephone calls to
SAMCO and to PBT Electronics
produced advice about not
screwing in too tight, replug-
ging in to cure corrosion,
keeping tight hold of the blue
ejection tab etc.

SAMCO insist on modest screwing
in; PBT say it is unnecessary -
except to stop the drives
falling out of the computer when
it is being carried. Eventually
I got the second drive to work
by a combination of very careful
plugging in and subsequent
fairly tight screwing in. Even
now,the second drive occasion-
ally goes on strike and has to
be laboriously re-installed.
When both drives work they are a
real treat.


[SAMCo have now sent a new disc
drive with an apology and asked
for the old drive to be returned
following a personal letter to
Alan Miles.]

My next ploy was to get my bread
and butter Spectrum software to
work, i.e. PCG, Masterfile,
Superfile, Artist 2, Artstudio,
Tasword 2, The Last Word and a
few utilities and snapshotted
games like chess and scrabble.

PCG was transferred painlessly
by slavishly following
Speclone's instructions for this
very program. Speclone has since
been left severely alone as I
cannot cope with the programming
required. All the rest were
handled with the greatest of
ease by Specmaker, a real boon
to ex-Spectrum users.

Regretfully, I did not manage
TASWORD 3, possibly because my

Plus 2 adaptation of it is not
as perfect as some of the later
ones; I can get it to print but
not to Load or Save.

TASWORD 2 presented some
difficulty at first because of
the ease of overlooking some of
several minor points. MOVE in
lines 279 & 281, deletion of the
POKE in line 280 (a tip from Nev
Young) and the adaptation to the
Euroelectronics ZXLprint inter-
face as advised in SPECMAKER.

With the disc drives and
emulators under control and
programs, text files, graphics
files all transferred, the next
step was to try some purpose
built SAM software.

FLASH, still being studied, does
not have rescaling facility;
OUTWRITE would be even more use-
ful if it had a better insert
facility; SC-FILER is useful
enough for me to have transfer-
red to it from Masterfile all my
telephone/address records, using
the model format already supp-
lied; making up one's own format
is not easy; one mistake means
restarting from scratch and
there is no means of recording
the specifications.

SAM DICE from Kobrahsoft is
first rate;it permits bulk copy-
ing of selected files, un-erase,
bulk erase,and the rearrangement
of files on a disc, to mention
just a few of its facilities.

It also permits the examination
of text files without loading
them into word processors and is
beautifully presented.


Lerm's Samdisk, similar, permits
the repair of damaged sectors.

Mrs. Carol Brooksbanks's MONEY
MANAGER has been bought as a
means of studying SAM BASIC when
the inclination comes.


FORMAT's game, DRAGON TILES
completes the collection so far.
Certainly not bad as a start but
a computer like SAM could
handle, say, a much better desk
top publishing facility.

One or two problems: A disk full
of Spectrum screen$ files has a
short viewer programme as
follows: 10 FOR n=1 TO 100 20
LOAD pn 30 PRINT AT 21,0;n 40
PAUSE 0: NEXT n. I can't find
the equivalent language in SAM
BASIC to make this work.

Mention is made in the Manual of
the DUMP command. Am I right in
assuming that this will not work
unless one loads in the machine
code routine from the Master
system disc? In my set-up, if it
is not loaded, nothing happens.

It also seems rather odd that
screendumps are in reverse - ink
wasted in printing in black what
should be white.

I miss the ready means available
on the Plus D of making a hard
copy or a screen$ file at the
drop of a hat by using the
snapshot button. Some screen$
files from FLASH, when loaded
independently, flash on and off
for some reason and I've disc-
overed no way of stopping this.

All this, admittedly, is only
scratching the surface. Without
a colour monitor I cannot
appreciate the improved colour
range and sound, the BASIC and
the vastly increased memory.

What about general reactions?
The shape of SAM is pleasant,
the disc drives are a dream - if
only they were better machined.

The keyboard is very pleasant to
handle and the function keys are
very useful - I have made myself
a small program to alter them
all. I should have preferred
beige or black to the glaring
whiteness of the machine.


The interfaces and the SAMBUS
are bulky to the point of being
unsightly. It is still early
days and there seems as yet very
little software which fully
exploits SAM's impressive
specifications.

The SAMCo staff are pleasant to
talk to but the firm does not
seem to have become just yet a
complete miracle of efficiency.

It took them six weeks to supply
a lead for a black and white
monitor. The receipt for the
computer and its attachments
were scribbled on blank paper
and could have been written by
anybody. The supplied mouse
version of FLASH does not work
and the twice promised replace-
ment has never arrived.

Retail outlets are few - there
are none in Glasgow - and funds
do not seem available for
advertisement. On the publicity
side,I'd like to know as a
matter of interest what ATARI
and AMIGA can do which SAM can
not, whether their 16-bit really
matters, in other words whether
one loses much in choosing SAM.

If not, this should be a very
good selling point.

The Sam is a pleasant, modestly
priced, no-nonsense computer to
operate and I should really like
to see it succeed.

                     - Ian Ross

Brian Cavers to Ian Ross

Many thanks, Ian.

The equivalent to the Disciple's
LOAD Pn is simple LOAD n but
Spectrum SCREEN$ will not load
from a Disciple or +D disc if
that is what you are trying to
do! At least, it won't with the
normal SAMDOS but it will with
MASTERDOS. If you are using
SAMDOS then you will need to
convert the screens first thus:-

On the Spectrum you will need to
load each screen by name with...
LOAD "NAME" SCREEN$ then resave
it with...

   SAVE "NAME" CODE 16384,6912

Naturally, you will need to
erase the first copy if saving
on the same disc or else you
will get a prompt that will wipe
out the bottom two lines of the
screen.

Once saved, they will have to be
loaded by name into SAM using...

       LOAD "NAME" SCREEN$

..but you MUST set Mode 1 first.

Finally, you can resave them
again from SAM using...

       SAVE "NAME" SCREEN$

          ...after which you can
load by directory number!

Yes, DUMP will not work unless
the code is loaded.There was not
enough room in ROM. SAM's DUMP
is only really suitable for a
black and white screen as it
makes a mess of most colours I'm
afraid!

Try MASTERDOS (from SAMCo) which
includes a choice of better
dumps in the DOS so you don't
need to load any extra code as
it loads when you boot DOS.


However, note that if you write
any programs using this facility
it will not work for people with
SAMDOS so make it optional to
include the usual DUMP and load
the old dump code.

In FLASH, if you change colours,
select "COLOUR OK" at the SCREEN
sub-menu before you save to cure
the flashing bug or load the
screen in ANTIFLASH(OUTLET 37).

Regarding the colour of SAM, it
has now been changed and new
machines are black or dark grey.

One of the standard screens on
both Amiga and ST are similar in
quality to SAM's Mode 4 and most
of the pictures in DEMOPIX are
from the Amiga and ST. However,
both machines have higher screen
modes and their processor is
faster than the SAM. This is
apparent in the high-speed with
complex graphics of games and
much faster graphics programs.

FLASH could be much improved, of
course, on SAM, for speed and
complexity but it will never be
as fast as can be achieved on
the Amiga and ST.

SAM's hardware is much easier to
access than the Amiga or ST so
programming in machine code is
far more comprehensible. Many
programmers have switched to the
16-bit machines and made little
progress there. I must stress
that programming the 68000 chip
is not harder (some say easier)
than the Z80 but it is accessing
the hardware that's complicated!

SAM's BASIC,though sadly bugged,
is more friendly than anything
I've seen on the ST and more
powerful in some areas.

I've been asked several times to
produce an OUTLET on the ST but
quite frankly, things you take
for granted on the Spectrum and
SAM are immensely difficult on
the ST and, I presume the Amiga.
It speaks for itself that my ST,
which I've had since they first
were produced, gathers dust and
is only used to extract screens
for DEMOPIX usually, whereas my
Spectrum and SAM take a real
pounding every day!

Finally, OUTWRITE's insert is so
easy to use but it does seem to
be misunderstand at times. Set
insert mode. Move to the point
where you want to insert. Hold
symbol and press cursor down.
Type as much as you want. Reform
the paragraph.         - Brian

From: Marc Broster, LINCS.

Dear Brian,

I thought I should write after
reading your reply to my letter
in OUTLET 52, regarding the
comment I made about not finding
OUTLET good value. It was only a
very small comment and I didn't
mean that OUTLET was over-priced
or that you should lower the
price or anything.

I realise that OUTLET takes up
all of your time, while other
SAM disc mags are only produced
as a hobby and, of course, you
pay vast sums (well ten pounds
is generous!) to people like me
for their contributions.

I think that for over `3.00 the
issues of OUTLET I have received
do not strike me as good value
for money. When I receive
OUTLET, I spend half an hour,
maybe three quarters, or even an
hour if there's loads of text,
loading up the various progs and
reading the bits of text, then
the disc gets banished to the
back off the disc box never to
be seen again.

You said that as I only receive
the odd issue of OUTLET, I might
be missing out, which is true.
Issue 37 (I think), one of the
first discs I received for my
SAM, contained the excellent
BASIC game SPRINGY THINGY, which
was great fun and probably the
best use of BASIC I have seen.

However, Issue 52 for example
was really poor by my standards,
the only program on the disc
(apart from the pics) to remind
me I was looking at a SAM
version of OUTLET rather than
the Speccy version, was my
(rather pathetic) ZARCH program.


I often swap letters with Phil
Glover (the Adventure Club
person), and in his letter Phil
mentioned mine in OUTLET. Like
yourself (and probably hundreds
of OUTLET fans), Phil said he
found OUTLET good value. One of
the points he raised was that
OUTLET is much better value than
newstand mags such as Crash or
YS, to which I disagree.

I recently realised I had a vast
sum of money in my bank account,
so I decided to buy a Mega Drive
and a few Mega Drive mags. My
fave is SEGA POWER, and despite
a daft name and usually naff
covers, there is usually enough
text inside to keep me reading
it for around a fortnight, which
I consider to be a good deal for
`1.75.

Phil also said we are spoilt for
choice with SAM mags such as the
SUPPLEMENT and FRED. I only
subscribe to the SUPPLEMENT as
it is practically free, and pick
up copies of FRED and ENCELADUS
as I can. I agree with Phil, if
the SUPPLEMENT, FRED,etc weren't
produced, I am sure I would put
in a regular order for OUTLET.

Geek, over 400 words! Anyway, I
hope now you can see my point of
view. I'd better draw to a close
or you'll have to devote the
entire OUTLETTERS section to me!

In OUTWRITE!, is there a POKE to
set Word Wrap to OFF from the
start? (there should be!). When
showing a quick DIR, Masterdos
automatically sorts the files
in order, so it takes a while to
see the last file you worked on.
Is there a POKE to stop this?

In Masterdos, if you use a full
stop, the file name gets padded
out with spaces, which makes
DIRs look neat but limits the
characters after a full stop to
three. Is there a way to stop
this?             - Marc Broster

Brian Cavers to Marc Broster

Thanks,Marc.I see your point of
view but what you really mean is
that OUTLET is not to your taste
-not that it is not good value.
That is a bit like someone who's
not interested in literature
saying that a `5 bundle of the
complete works of Shakespeare is
not good value.  Personally, I'd
gladly pay `5 or `10 for many of
the programs that have appeared
in OUTLET on their own but what
are YOU looking for?

You say OUTLET 52 was poor and
that it looked like a "Speccy"
version! You must look with your
eyes closed!Let me be your guide
dog...

Boot the disc and you see a demo
which would have been a strong
contender for our competition if
I hadn't disqualified myself! It
could never be done on the
Spectrum - it is in full colour
with a multitude of screens for
the snowfall effect!

The CONTENTS page - again,absurd
to think you could even get near
it on a Spectrum. The same goes
for BALLOONS, BARSCROLL, all our
text pages, DEMOPIX and you
could not possibly do justice to
THE MUSICIAN in less than a day
of experimenting nor read all of
the text let alone absorb all
that information! Be honest, you
never studied the articles and
letters fully!

If I walk in W.H. Smiths I see
hundreds and hundreds of magaz-
ines covering fishing, music,
climbing, dogs, cats, fashion,
you name it! Because 99% of them
do not interest me does not mean
they are poor value! If I pick
up a copy of SEGA POWER it will
hold my interest for about three
minutes but it would never occur
to me to think of it as poor
value just because there is
nothing there for me.

I guess all this really boils
down to a poor choice of words
on your part when you meant
something totally different but
you can't blame me for defending
the fruits of over four years
labour and hardship.

Now on to more interesting items
in your letter! Yes, you can set
WORDWRAP OFF as the default in
OUTWRITE and any of the other
settings. Just enter the text
editor, set all the features how
you want them and then exit to
the menu with EDIT and Q and use
the SAVE option. When you next
load that copy you will find
everything set how you want it -
even CAPS ON if you want it!

To cancel the alphabetical sort
of a MASTERDOS DIR use...

          POKE DVAR 9,0

To restore it to alpha sort use

          POKE DVAR 9,1

To cancel the MASTERDOS DIR 1
"spacing out" to a full stop in
a filename use...

         POKE DVAR 11,0

I agree that the normal spacing
can be awkward and limits the
suffix to three characters. It
also makes it impossible to see
the real filename of any file
with more than three characters
after the suffix as I know after
much head-banging! Still, there
are loads of DVARs to customise
MASTERDOS how you want it!

Anyway,I hope that helps and you
stop with OUTLET if only for the
useful info!
                        - Brian.

From: R.J. Fox, SUFFOLK


Dear Sirs,

In the March 1983 edition of
Your Computer, a Mr Rod Hopkins
contributed a very interesting
article which enabled the
Spectrum to generate minuets at
random from tables composed by
Mozart.

In order to do this with the
three sound channels required,
Mr Hopkins had to use a piece of
add-on hardware.

The program also had the ability
to display and produce printouts
of the music it had generated.

It seems to me that, in view of
the improved sound capability of
SAM and also of the recent
Mozart bicentenary, the time is
ripe for a SAM version of this
program.

What about it, Mr. Hopkins? Are
you out there somewhere? Or is
there anyone else who could
undertake this?

        Yours faithfully,

             R.J.FOX


Have we any child prodigies in
our midst who can spare us a few
minuets of their time?
                       - Brian

SAM disc drives. A reader
comments in Issue 53 that he
gets "check disc in drive"
error. Interesting! I have been
getting this strange report from
time to time. It happens on
drive 2 and seems to be at the
first time of use. At the second
time of use - all O.K. from then
on, i.e., BOOT, DIR2 (get error
report). do nothing mechanical
such as remove and re-enter disc
or give drive a "thump" simply
retype DIR2 and all will be O.K.

I have V2 of SAMDOS and V3 rom.
The problem is also same with
MASTERDOS V2.1

I have yet to prove conclusively
but it does seem to connect with
having used the RESET button on
the back. The problem seems to
be able to be induced if the
RESET is released too soon.
Pressing and holding for say 3
seconds seems to be O.K.

I also get from time to time a
change in the way FORMAT works
for no known reason.(MASTERDOS
loaded I believe) e.g., BOOT and
then FORMAT, sometimes I get the
"are you sure" prompt, sometimes
it formats straight off without
the prompt.

(I altered OUTWRITE FORMAT to
give a second chance to exit for
this reason, as if selected in
error it would sometimes go
straight into a format! on the
wrong disc!"

Now a second example: A number
of discs to be formatted. Use a
routine such as

10 FORMAT 1
20 FORMAT 2
30 GOTO 10

on RUN it formats discs in D1
and D2 alternatively WITHOUT any
"are you sure" prompt for say 7
discs then the 8th gives the
"are you sure prompt" 9 and on
continue to format without.

Using the above routine if a
disc is left out and it has been
formatting without the prompt
then when it stops with 'error
due to missing disc' from then
on it seems to have restored the
"are you sure" prompt for every
disc following. Has anybody else
noticed this?

What does get on my wick is when
SAM returns from doing a disc
operation with the report "OK"
when in fact it's done nothing.

I have just formatted a disc and
waited while it verified and got
"OK" when the disc was write
protected, so in fact while it
was formatting it was simply
spinning the disc and not a lot
else.

It verified because the disc was
already formatted and all
sectors intact.

I also get "OK" for saves when
nothing has actually been saved
due to disc being write
protected. An easy way to lose
data if you take SAM's word that
it did an "OK" save.

I did have a scan through the
various system data info to see
if perhaps there was a DOS
variable set to inhibit the
error report to say disc write
protected but so far I have not
found one if there is.

          Malcolm Perry

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry

The new SCPDSA disc will be `4
for 4 discs (sent each quarter)
+`1 post in Europe or `1.50 the
rest of the world. The `4 is
reduced to `3.50 when you renew.

However, as raised before in
these pages, although named as a
"public domain" association,this
is misleading. Please check
carefully before making copies
for friends or sending to your
favourite PD library because
some (most?) is definitely not
public domain but remains the
copyright of the software
producer whose rights must be
respected. No,I don't understand
it either!

If PRIMUS supply the two discs
and postage for their two-disc
magazine then they are doing
well! Even if they can get discs
at 30p each and use second-class
post it will cost 30p+30p+18p=
78p + say, 4p for an envelope =
82p! So, FORGETTING all over-
heads such as office supplies,
electricity and phone bills,
paying taxes, keeping accounts,
repairs, paying contributors for
the software they send replacing
bad discs returned, labels,
queries, cost of review software
and so on and on then if they
sell 100 issues they will make a
profit of `18. The truth is they
must operate at a loss at that
price and so either YOU send the
discs with an SAE or it is a
one-off, first-time offer.

The "check disc in drive" error
with drive 2 is common and I've
suffered it for a long time. It
happens with SAMDOS or MASTERDOS
but can be alleviated, as you
say, if when you reset, you hold
the button for several seconds.

This doesn't always work but I
recently noticed that if I keep
repeatedly resetting, eventually
the red light on my drive 2
comes on so I am deliberately
doing this to see if this cures
the problem absolutely.


So far, I have not known the bug
occur after a "red-light reset"
so it looks hopeful although a
real pain to have to do this!

I was unable to duplicate your
error with FORMAT running on a
write-protected disc. I got the
"disc write-protected" message
with both SAMDOS and MASTERDOS.

Regarding the lack of an "are
you sure?" message before FORMAT
with MASTERDOS, are you aware
that MASTERDOS does not ask for
confirmation if you try to
format a new, UNFORMATTED disc
(or one with an alien format)but
only asks if it detects a disc
that is previously formatted (as
does the Opus Discovery). It may
also regard a Disciple disc as
an "alien" format.

Thanks for the various bits of
info, Malcolm.
                        - Brian

From: William Coats,STRATHCLYDE

Dear Brian/Ron,

As this is my first letter to
you let me start off by thanking
you for such a great "magazine"
and, after your recent price
restructuring, a great bargain!

Re: your answer to D. Green of
Sheffield about Fontwist.2 (OUT-
LET 51) you asked for feedback
on loading and downloading of
fonts on printers.

My set up is a +3 (the one that
needs POKEs to 23354/23355) and
a Citizen 120D+ printer. I
managed to get your program to
load the fonts into the printer
- with one or two alterations...

Line 1105 (the attr byte) has to
go before line 1100.

Line 6200 to read...

6200 GO SUB 9886: FOR a=33536 TO
33536+(L-1) : PRINT AT 10,13;A:
LPRINT CHR$ PEEK A;: NEXT A
(the PRINT in the line lets you
see the bytes downloading.

Line 9895 becomes 9896.

Insert new line...

9895 LPRINT CHR$(27);":";CHR$(0)
;CHR$(0);CHR$(0)
(this copies the current font in
ROM to RAM and so can be altered
- if you want to alter just a
few characters.

On the 120D+ you have to rotate
anti-clockwise and mirror. Each
character is made up on a matrix
6 columns wide by 9 rows deep,
so you have 6 dots in a row plus
5 dots in the lines between the
columns. The limitation on the
120D+ is that you cannot define
a character which has two
immediately-adjacent dots, i.e.
one in a box and one on the line
next to it, in the same row.

Now for my problem! If I reset
the computer, load in a program
for printing, the printer
doesn't operate. But if I BREAK
back to BASIC then RUN the
program again it works fine. Is

## Letterc3

E V E N   M O R E   M A I L !

From: Iain Ross

LEARNING TO LIVE WITH SAM

SAM was brought to my notice first by its rapturous welcome by FORMAT which seemed to hail it as the 'Second Coming' and then by a series of decidedly salty comments from OUTLET. My decision not to buy what looked like a can of worms was overcome partly by very full information and advice from one of FORMAT's leading contributors and partly by the growing feeling that the Spectrum is inevitably, and sadly, destined for oblivion. A walk down Tottenham Court Road last summer yielded not a trace of the Spectrum nor any of its accessories or software.

Needless to say, Ataris and Amigas proliferated but buying one would have lost me my Specrum software. So last September, at the Glasgow All Formats Fair, I took the plunge and treated myself to a 512K SAM, two disc drives, a 1 Mb extension, printer extension, a mouse, Masterdos, Specmaker and Speclone.

I use a computer essentially as a piece of office equipment, also as a means of indulging my fondness for graphic art and typography. Lacking technical expertise and with no real prog- ramming ability, I anticipated lots of trouble and frustration.

In fact, apart from trouble with a disc drive, virtually nothing went wrong.

Not a keen computer buff, I left SAM BASIC alone. Fascinated by the extremely compact discdrives hidden inside the computer, I made these the first object of my attention. One of the drives worked; the other worked only sporadically.

Numerous telephone calls to SAMCO and to PBT Electronics produced advice about not screwing in too tight, replug- ging in to cure corrosion, keeping tight hold of the blue ejection tab etc.

SAMCO insist on modest screwing in; PBT say it is unnecessary - except to stop the drives falling out of the computer when it is being carried. Eventually I got the second drive to work by a combination of very careful plugging in and subsequent fairly tight screwing in. Even now,the second drive occasion- ally goes on strike and has to be laboriously re-installed. When both drives work they are a real treat.

[SAMCo have now sent a new disc drive with an apology and asked for the old drive to be returned following a personal letter to Alan Miles.]

My next ploy was to get my bread and butter Spectrum software to work, i.e. PCG, Masterfile, Superfile, Artist 2, Artstudio, Tasword 2, The Last Word and a few utilities and snapshotted games like chess and scrabble.

PCG was transferred painlessly by slavishly following Speclone's instructions for this very program. Speclone has since been left severely alone as I cannot cope with the programming required. All the rest were handled with the greatest of ease by Specmaker, a real boon to ex-Spectrum users.

Regretfully, I did not manage TASWORD 3, possibly because my

Plus 2 adaptation of it is not as perfect as some of the later ones; I can get it to print but not to Load or Save.

TASWORD 2 presented some difficulty at first because of the ease of overlooking some of several minor points. MOVE in lines 279 & 281, deletion of the POKE in line 280 (a tip from Nev Young) and the adaptation to the Euroelectronics ZXLprint inter- face as advised in SPECMAKER.

With the disc drives and emulators under control and programs, text files, graphics files all transferred, the next step was to try some purpose built SAM software.

FLASH, still being studied, does not have rescaling facility; OUTWRITE would be even more use- ful if it had a better insert facility; SC-FILER is useful enough for me to have transfer- red to it from Masterfile all my telephone/address records, using the model format already supp- lied; making up one's own format is not easy; one mistake means restarting from scratch and there is no means of recording the specifications.

SAM DICE from Kobrahsoft is first rate;it permits bulk copy- ing of selected files, un-erase, bulk erase,and the rearrangement of files on a disc, to mention just a few of its facilities.

It also permits the examination of text files without loading them into word processors and is beautifully presented.

Lerm's Samdisk, similar, permits the repair of damaged sectors.

Mrs. Carol Brooksbanks's MONEY MANAGER has been bought as a means of studying SAM BASIC when the inclination comes.

FORMAT's game, DRAGON TILES completes the collection so far. Certainly not bad as a start but a computer like SAM could handle, say, a much better desk top publishing facility.

One or two problems: A disk full of Spectrum screen$ files has a short viewer programme as follows: 10 FOR n=1 TO 100 20 LOAD pn 30 PRINT AT 21,0;n 40 PAUSE 0: NEXT n. I can't find the equivalent language in SAM BASIC to make this work.

Mention is made in the Manual of the DUMP command. Am I right in assuming that this will not work unless one loads in the machine code routine from the Master system disc? In my set-up, if it is not loaded, nothing happens.

It also seems rather odd that screendumps are in reverse - ink wasted in printing in black what should be white.

I miss the ready means available on the Plus D of making a hard copy or a screen$ file at the drop of a hat by using the snapshot button. Some screen$ files from FLASH, when loaded independently, flash on and off for some reason and I've disc- overed no way of stopping this.

All this, admittedly, is only scratching the surface. Without a colour monitor I cannot appreciate the improved colour range and sound, the BASIC and the vastly increased memory.

What about general reactions? The shape of SAM is pleasant, the disc drives are a dream - if only they were better machined.

The keyboard is very pleasant to handle and the function keys are very useful - I have made myself a small program to alter them all. I should have preferred beige or black to the glaring whiteness of the machine.

The interfaces and the SAMBUS are bulky to the point of being unsightly. It is still early days and there seems as yet very little software which fully exploits SAM's impressive specifications.

The SAMCo staff are pleasant to talk to but the firm does not seem to have become just yet a complete miracle of efficiency.

It took them six weeks to supply a lead for a black and white monitor. The receipt for the computer and its attachments were scribbled on blank paper and could have been written by anybody. The supplied mouse version of FLASH does not work and the twice promised replace- ment has never arrived.

Retail outlets are few - there are none in Glasgow - and funds do not seem available for advertisement. On the publicity side,I'd like to know as a matter of interest what ATARI and AMIGA can do which SAM can not, whether their 16-bit really matters, in other words whether one loses much in choosing SAM.

If not, this should be a very good selling point.

The Sam is a pleasant, modestly priced, no-nonsense computer to operate and I should really like to see it succeed.

- Ian Ross

Brian Cavers to Ian Ross

Many thanks, Ian.

The equivalent to the Disciple's LOAD Pn is simple LOAD n but Spectrum SCREEN$ will not load from a Disciple or +D disc if that is what you are trying to do! At least, it won't with the normal SAMDOS but it will with MASTERDOS. If you are using SAMDOS then you will need to convert the screens first thus:-

On the Spectrum you will need to load each screen by name with... LOAD "NAME" SCREEN$ then resave it with...

SAVE "NAME" CODE 16384,6912

Naturally, you will need to erase the first copy if saving on the same disc or else you will get a prompt that will wipe out the bottom two lines of the screen.

Once saved, they will have to be loaded by name into SAM using...

LOAD "NAME" SCREEN$

..but you MUST set Mode 1 first.

Finally, you can resave them again from SAM using...

SAVE "NAME" SCREEN$

...after which you can load by directory number!

Yes, DUMP will not work unless the code is loaded.There was not enough room in ROM. SAM's DUMP is only really suitable for a black and white screen as it makes a mess of most colours I'm afraid!

Try MASTERDOS (from SAMCo) which includes a choice of better dumps in the DOS so you don't need to load any extra code as it loads when you boot DOS.

However, note that if you write any programs using this facility it will not work for people with SAMDOS so make it optional to include the usual DUMP and load the old dump code.

In FLASH, if you change colours, select "COLOUR OK" at the SCREEN sub-menu before you save to cure the flashing bug or load the screen in ANTIFLASH(OUTLET 37).

Regarding the colour of SAM, it has now been changed and new machines are black or dark grey.

One of the standard screens on both Amiga and ST are similar in quality to SAM's Mode 4 and most of the pictures in DEMOPIX are from the Amiga and ST. However, both machines have higher screen modes and their processor is faster than the SAM. This is apparent in the high-speed with complex graphics of games and much faster graphics programs.

FLASH could be much improved, of course, on SAM, for speed and complexity but it will never be as fast as can be achieved on the Amiga and ST.

SAM's hardware is much easier to access than the Amiga or ST so programming in machine code is far more comprehensible. Many programmers have switched to the 16-bit machines and made little progress there. I must stress that programming the 68000 chip is not harder (some say easier) than the Z80 but it is accessing the hardware that's complicated!

SAM's BASIC,though sadly bugged, is more friendly than anything I've seen on the ST and more powerful in some areas.

I've been asked several times to produce an OUTLET on the ST but quite frankly, things you take for granted on the Spectrum and SAM are immensely difficult on the ST and, I presume the Amiga. It speaks for itself that my ST, which I've had since they first were produced, gathers dust and is only used to extract screens for DEMOPIX usually, whereas my Spectrum and SAM take a real pounding every day!

Finally, OUTWRITE's insert is so easy to use but it does seem to be misunderstand at times. Set insert mode. Move to the point where you want to insert. Hold symbol and press cursor down. Type as much as you want. Reform the paragraph.         - Brian

From: Marc Broster, LINCS.

Dear Brian,

I thought I should write after reading your reply to my letter in OUTLET 52, regarding the comment I made about not finding OUTLET good value. It was only a very small comment and I didn't mean that OUTLET was over-priced or that you should lower the price or anything.

I realise that OUTLET takes up all of your time, while other SAM disc mags are only produced as a hobby and, of course, you pay vast sums (well ten pounds is generous!) to people like me for their contributions.

Brian Cavers to Marc Broster

Thanks,Marc.I see your point of view but what you really mean is that OUTLET is not to your taste -not that it is not good value. That is a bit like someone who's not interested in literature saying that a `5 bundle of the complete works of Shakespeare is not good value.  Personally, I'd gladly pay `5 or `10 for many of the programs that have appeared in OUTLET on their own but what are YOU looking for?

You say OUTLET 52 was poor and that it looked like a "Speccy" version! You must look with your eyes closed!Let me be your guide dog...

Boot the disc and you see a demo which would have been a strong contender for our competition if I hadn't disqualified myself! It could never be done on the Spectrum - it is in full colour with a multitude of screens for the snowfall effect!

The CONTENTS page - again,absurd to think you could even get near it on a Spectrum. The same goes for BALLOONS, BARSCROLL, all our text pages, DEMOPIX and you could not possibly do justice to THE MUSICIAN in less than a day of experimenting nor read all of the text let alone absorb all that information! Be honest, you never studied the articles and letters fully!

If I walk in W.H. Smiths I see hundreds and hundreds of magaz- ines covering fishing, music, climbing, dogs, cats, fashion, you name it! Because 99% of them do not interest me does not mean they are poor value! If I pick up a copy of SEGA POWER it will hold my interest for about three minutes but it would never occur to me to think of it as poor value just because there is nothing there for me.

I guess all this really boils down to a poor choice of words on your part when you meant something totally different but you can't blame me for defending the fruits of over four years labour and hardship.

Now on to more interesting items in your letter! Yes, you can set WORDWRAP OFF as the default in OUTWRITE and any of the other settings. Just enter the text editor, set all the features how you want them and then exit to the menu with EDIT and Q and use the SAVE option. When you next load that copy you will find everything set how you want it - even CAPS ON if you want it!

To cancel the alphabetical sort of a MASTERDOS DIR use...

POKE DVAR 9,0

To restore it to alpha sort use

POKE DVAR 9,1

To cancel the MASTERDOS DIR 1 "spacing out" to a full stop in a filename use...

POKE DVAR 11,0

I agree that the normal spacing can be awkward and limits the suffix to three characters. It also makes it impossible to see the real filename of any file with more than three characters after the suffix as I know after much head-banging! Still, there are loads of DVARs to customise MASTERDOS how you want it!

Anyway,I hope that helps and you stop with OUTLET if only for the useful info!

### УЧИМСЯ ЖИТЬ С SAM

Поэтому в сентябре прошлого года, на выставке Glasgow All Formats Fair, я решился и побаловал себя 512K SAM, двумя дисководами, расширением на 1 Мб, расширением для принтера, мышью, Masterdos, Specmaker и Speclone.

Я использую компьютер по существу как предмет офисного оборудования, а также как средство для потакания моей страсти к графике и типографике. Не обладая техническими знаниями и какими-либо реальными навыками программирования, я ожидал массу проблем и разочарований.

Sam — это приятный, скромно оцененный, серьезный компьютер для работы, и я очень хотел бы, чтобы он преуспел.

```text
6200 GO SUB 9886: FOR a=33536 TO 33536+(L-1) : PRINT AT 10,13;A: LPRINT CHR$ PEEK A;: NEXT A
```

```text
9895 LPRINT CHR$(27);":";CHR$(0);CHR$(0);CHR$(0)
```
